section.sectionSummaryBrief: The sin of the Tree of Knowledge caused a mixture of good and evil, which is brought about by the faculty of Daat.
section.t: Now, it is known that the sin of the Tree of Knowledge brought about the matter of the mixture of good and evil,
as explained in the sicha of my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, from Yud-Tes Kislev,
that in every single thing there is a mixture of good and evil, and there is no good without evil,
and there is no evil without good,
as is known,
that after the sin of the Tree of Knowledge, every thing in the world is in a manner of mixture of good and evil.
And this matter is from the aspect of Daat,
for, behold,
one who has no Daat at all, or who has only smallness of Daat,
goes along in his simple way,
meaning,
that everything he does is in utmost simplicity without any admixture of the opposite thing,
for when he does a good thing, no evil is mixed into it,
and when he does an evil thing, no good is mixed into it,
because he has no Daat or cunning,
but unlike him, one who has Daat and cunning,
who can conceal himself
(he can hide himself),
then it is possible that in doing the thing he will have some intention or ulterior motive and the like,
so that then, even when externally he does a good thing,
nevertheless,
it can be that internally it is an evil thing,
and likewise the opposite, that externally it is evil and internally it is good.
And along the lines of what is said,
"He who spares his rod hates his son,"
that even though outwardly it is a matter of Gevurah, that he chastises his son,
nevertheless, from the perspective of the intention in this, it is a matter of Chessed,
for he does this out of his love for his son,
and this means,
that even though from the perspective of his love for his son he wants only to benefit him with revealed good,
nevertheless,
through Daat, there is a strengthening of the intellect to incline the attribute,
because he delves and understands that even though he loves his son,
nevertheless,
for his benefit he needs to chastise him,
and through this an inclination toward Gevurah is generated in him,
and from the inclination to the attribute of Gevurah,
afterward he comes to openly chastise his son.
And this is the matter of the sin of the Tree of Knowledge,
that the matter of Daat brings about a mixture of good and evil.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The kelipot lack inner Daat but possess external Daat, which enables mixture, as Daat brings about detail and inter-inclusion.
section.t: But one must understand,
for the kelipot have no brain of Daat,
as it is stated in the Zohar,
"The Other God is a eunuch and does not produce fruit, etc."
And the explanation of this is,
that this lack of Daat refers to the innerness of Daat,
which brings about nullification in the emotions,
from which there is no sustenance for the Other Side,
but they possess the externality of Daat,
from which there can be sustenance for the Other Side,
and through this a mixture of good and evil is brought about.
And the matter is,
behold,
the matter of mixture applies only when there are details,
and as the Mitteler Rebbe said,
that regarding the four elements as they are in themselves, the matter of inter-inclusion does not apply to them,
and only from the aspect that the element of fire also contains the element of water, and the element of water also contains the element of fire, etc.,
therefore the matter of inter-inclusion applies.
And so it is with the matter of Daat,
that because it is the matter of depth, through which the intellect comes in a multiplicity of details,
therefore it brings about the matter of inter-inclusion and mixture.
And this is not a contradiction to what is explained elsewhere,
that the multiplicity of details in the intellect come through Binah,
for,
from the perspective of Binah, the details exist only in a general way,
but unlike this, when one understands through the depth that is in the power of Daat,
then the matter comes in the most particular details, etc.
And this is the advantage of Daat over the intellects of Chochmah and Binah,
for, behold, in the intellect in general there is length, width, and depth,
length is the matter of the point of Chochmah,
meaning that the essential rationale as it is drawn down and descends from level to level,
only that it is in the aspect of enclothing, etc.
And width is the matter of Binah, which details the details in the intellect,
but this is still in a general way.
And afterward comes the matter of depth, which is the matter of Daat,
that from the aspect of depth, the true matter of details is brought about,
for one finds in the intellect all the most particular details within it,
and from this, inter-inclusion and mixture can occur.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: Daat both causes mixture and enables discernment to separate good from evil, especially to refine the subtle evil.
section.t: However, based on this, one must understand what the Targum says on the verse,
"the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil,"
"from which the wise eat, discerning between good and evil,"
meaning,
that through Daat one can discern, separate, and distinguish between good and evil.
And as it is brought in the Gemara,
that because of this they established Havdalah in "Chonen HaDaat" (the blessing for knowledge),
for if there is no Daat, from where is separation, etc.
And here it is explained the opposite,
that through Daat a mixture of good and evil is brought about.
But the matter is,
behold,
when evil is revealed and coarse,
then the work of discerning it, etc., is not so difficult,
and one does not specifically need the brain of Daat for this.
However,
since through the sin of the Tree of Knowledge a mixture of good and evil was brought about in the world,
and also the subtlety of evil was brought about,
behold, for this there is a need for work with exertion specifically
(and through this, "and you will find"),
to discern even the subtlety of evil and to extract the good from the evil.
And the matter in this,
behold, it is written,
"Cords of emptiness and like ropes of a cart, sin,"
meaning,
that if at first there were no cords of emptiness,
it would be impossible to come to sin, which is like the ropes of a cart,
for how is it possible that one would do such a thing,
and only through that at first there were cords of emptiness,
which is the matter of the subtlety of evil,
behold, from this one comes afterward to the ropes of a cart, sin,
the coarseness of evil.
But in order to discern the subtlety of evil and to refine it, one must exert oneself more,
and as is known,
Yaakov was in the house of Lavan for twenty years in order to refine even the subtlety of evil,
but unlike this, regarding Eisav, a great amount of time was not needed,
because in Eisav there was only the coarseness of evil.
And this matter is accomplished through the brain of Daat,
and this means,
from the aspect of the expanse of Daat,
that one enters into the depth of the thing and knows all its details
(from which very aspect inter-inclusion and mixture of good and evil come about, as above),
he has the power to discern even the subtlety of evil and to extract the good from the evil.
